Listen to this article Share The Nigerian Exchange (NGX) on Wednesday hosted the AT50 Lagos Market Open, bringing together regulators, investment bankers and technology company founders to discuss how African businesses can attract more institutional investment and access public capital. Advertisement Advertisement The event, held at the NGX House on Customs Street, Lagos, was organised by Indexa Exchange Group, with Standard Bank as lead partner. It brought the financing needs of Africa’s growing technology companies into focus, particularly the challenge of moving beyond venture capital and attracting funding from larger institutional investors. Nigeria has 16 companies represented in the AT50 Index, the highest number of any African country. The index tracks some of the continent’s leading private technology businesses and provides a platform for greater visibility among investors. Among the key participants listed for the event were Securities and Exchange Commission Director-General Emomotimi Agama, NGX Group chief executive Temi Popoola, NGX chief executive Jude Chiemeka and Indexa chairman Gbite Oduneye. Technology founders included Olugbenga Agboola of Flutterwave, Tayo Oviosu of Paga, Babs Ogundeyi of Kuda and Ridwan Olalere of LemFi. Advertisement Discussions at the event were centred on the ability of African technology companies to attract long-term funding, strengthen corporate governance and prepare their businesses for institutional investment and possible stock market listings. Read also: Anthropic IPO draws strong demand as AI company prepares for $64bn share sale Advertisement For many technology companies, raising funds through venture capital has been an important part of their growth. However, as these businesses expand, their financing needs also increase, creating demand for larger pools of capital. This presents an opportunity for African exchanges, including the NGX, to attract businesses that may eventually seek funding through public markets rather than depend solely on private investors. Advertisement Advertisement The AT50 initiative is intended to increase the visibility of leading African private companies and connect them with investors and financial institutions. However, inclusion in the index does not automatically mean that a company is preparing for an initial public offering. The event places the country’s technology businesses and capital market in the same conversation at a time when the exchange is looking to broaden the range of companies and sectors represented on its platform. The larger question is whether African capital markets can provide the funding, liquidity and investor confidence needed to support the next stage of growth for the continent’s technology companies.
